Q6111.L1t: The First Amendment limits government restrictions on speech, and it applies to state and city governments through the Fourteenth Amendment.
Q6111.L2t: The Supreme Court has recognized that some expressive conduct, such as wearing armbands or burning a flag, can count as symbolic speech.
Q6111.L3t: A littering ban applies to everyone whatever message they intend, and the city's interest in clean parks has nothing to do with the protestor's message, so any burden on expression is incidental and the ordinance passes intermediate scrutiny.
Q6111.L4t: The protestor may be prosecuted, because the ordinance is content-neutral, serves a substantial government interest, and is not aimed at suppressing expression.
Q6111.L2f: The Supreme Court first recognized the idea of symbolic speech in a case about a tax on newspaper advertising revenue.
Q6111.L3f: The First Amendment protects only spoken or written words, so a physical act like dumping trash falls outside its scope however much the actor means to communicate by it.
Q6111.L4f: The protestor may be prosecuted, because dumping trash is an act rather than expression and so cannot be treated as communication.

Q8262.L1t: A confidence interval for a difference in two population proportions estimates how far apart the true proportions of the two groups are.
Q8262.L2t: The interval was built by subtracting the female sample proportion from the male sample proportion, using samples of 120 men and 100 women.
Q8262.L3t: Because the interval is male minus female and lies entirely below zero, every plausible value of the difference has the male proportion smaller than the female proportion.
Q8262.L4t: The interval indicates, with 95 percent confidence, that women favor Sunday shopping at a higher rate than men do.
Q8262.L2f: A 95 percent confidence interval for a difference in proportions is valid only when both samples are exactly the same size.
Q8262.L3f: An interval whose endpoints are close together, as with one this narrow, means the two population proportions are essentially the same.
Q8262.L4f: The interval shows that men and women are equally interested in shopping on Sundays.

Q6181.L1t: Child mortality worldwide has fallen substantially since 1990, though millions of children under five still die every year.
Q6181.L2t: Most deaths of children under five occur in low-income countries, especially in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
Q6181.L3t: In 2017 global burden estimates, the single leading cause of under-five deaths was an infectious illness of the lungs that killed more than 800,000 children, ahead of neonatal conditions.
Q6181.L4t: Infections of the lower airways, such as pneumonia, were the leading cause of death in children under five in 2017.
Q6181.L2f: Worldwide, about 25 million children under five died in 2017.
Q6181.L3f: Neonatal deaths make up most under-five deaths, and in 2017 estimates complications from being born too early killed more children than any single infectious disease did.
Q6181.L4f: Complications of preterm birth were the leading cause of death in children under five in 2017.
